segments.heading: EN.CSS Vue
segments.text: is a set of Vue 3 components for the EN.CSS framework. Each component is a thin binding: it renders the real markup and the ARIA attribute contract that the EN.CSS stylesheets read, and adds the behavior that CSS cannot provide (keyboard navigation, focus handling, state, remote data).

segments.heading: Principles
segments.text: EN.CSS does the looks. The components ship no component CSS (the only exceptions are small additions, such as the combobox clear button). Load the EN.CSS stylesheets each component lists under its requirements. State lives in attributes. , , , , and friends drive the styles, so the markup stays valid and inspectable. Native first. The modal is a real ; tabs follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern; the combobox follows the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern. Controlled and uncontrolled. Where it makes sense, a component works with or keeps its own state. Headless escape hatches. Behavior is also available as composables ( , , ). TypeScript first. Every prop, option and payload is typed and exported.

segments.heading: Hosts and namespaces
segments.text: The programmatic API is split in two halves that share a namespace (a string, unless you pass one): the host, , renders the modals of that namespace. Props on the host are defaults for every modal it renders (for example ). the composable, , puts modals into that namespace. Precedence, from lowest to highest: host props, , then the options of one call. Keep to one host per namespace. Two hosts would render every modal twice, and a development build warns about it. A modal opened before any host is mounted waits in the store and appears when a host mounts (a warning is printed in development).

segments.heading: Sidebar Menu
segments.text: is a sidebar navigation menu: an inline list of links with groups, badges, nested submenus and an optional icon-only rail with flyouts. Requires from .

segments.heading: Basic usage
segments.text: In an application, give leaves a (router) or (plain link). An item without a target renders as a button.

segments.heading: Parents
segments.text: A parent without , or with , is a that only opens and closes. A parent with is a link: a click navigates and flips its open state.

segments.heading: Open state
segments.text: Omit to let the menu manage it. accepts keys or . Ancestors of the active item open automatically ( ). With , only one group per level stays open.

segments.heading: Collapsed rail
segments.text: turns the menu into an icon rail ( ). Top-level items get an and a (from , or the label). Open state is left untouched while collapsed and applies again when expanded. Two flyout implementations: Behaviour (default) A CSS-only popup. Zero JavaScript, but it can be clipped by an on a scrollable sidebar Submenus and tooltips are driven by (loaded lazily): , flip/shift at the viewport edge, Escape to close, one flyout open at a time. Without popkit the CSS flyout is used and a development warning is printed Popkit keyboard: Enter/Space opens and pins a flyout, → opens it and focuses the first item, ↑/↓/Home/End move inside it, ← or Escape closes it and returns focus to the button.
